entities.summary:
Ottaviano degli Ubaldini was an Italian cardinal, often known in his own time as simply Il Cardinale, born into a wealthy and influential family in the 13th century.















 Ottaviano degli Ubaldini was a key figure in the Catholic Church during the Late Middle Ages, serving as a cardinal and participating in the election of multiple popes. He played a significant role in the politics of the Church, particularly during the papacy of Pope Urban IV, with whom he collaborated on several initiatives.




 Ottaviano degli Ubaldini's legacy is tied to the Catholic Church, as he was a key player in the Church's governance and policy-making during the 13th century. His influence can still be seen in the Church's modern-day structures and practices.


 Ottaviano degli Ubaldini's life is a testament to the complexities and nuances of the Catholic Church's history, offering valuable insights into the Church's role in shaping European society during the Middle Ages.
